name: GL Account Classification
description: Classify the general-ledger account affected by a business event into one of six classes (asset, liability, equity, revenue, expense, cogs). Correct classification drives financial statements, so contra accounts, accruals and inventory-cost conventions are the usual failure points for models that pattern-match on words like "expense" or "payable".
system_prompt:
You classify accounts under accrual accounting. Classes:
- asset: resources owned that will give future benefit (cash, receivables, inventory, prepaids, equipment).
- liability: obligations owed to others (payables, accrued expenses, unearned revenue, loans, taxes owed).
- equity: owners' residual interest (capital, retained earnings, owner draws, dividends declared charged to equity).
- revenue: income earned from operations or other gains.
- expense: costs of operating the business other than the cost of goods sold (wages, rent, depreciation, insurance expense, freight-out).
- cogs: cost of the goods sold, and under the PERIODIC inventory system the purchases and freight-in accounts that make up that cost.
Rules: Classify the PRIMARY account affected as asked in the input ("the debit side", "the credit side", or "the account named X"). A contra account takes the class of the account it offsets (accumulated depreciation is asset; sales returns is revenue; treasury stock is equity). Under the PERPETUAL inventory system purchases and freight-in are debited to Inventory (asset). Accrued items are recognised when earned or incurred, not when cash moves.
decision must be one of "asset","liability","equity","revenue","expense","cogs".
Respond with ONLY a JSON object: {"decision": <value>, "confidence": <0..1>, "reason": "<one sentence>"}

decision.instructions: Under accrual accounting, which class is the PRIMARY account the input asks about ("the debit side", "the credit side", or "the account named X")? A contra account takes the class of the account it offsets (accumulated depreciation is asset; sales returns is revenue; treasury stock is equity). Under the PERPETUAL inventory system, purchases and freight-in are debited to Inventory (asset); under PERIODIC they are cogs. Accrued items are recognised when earned or incurred, not when cash moves.

criteria.asset: Resources owned that give future benefit (cash, receivables, inventory, prepaids, equipment) and their contra accounts.
criteria.liability: Obligations owed to others (payables, accrued expenses, unearned revenue, loans, taxes owed).
criteria.equity: Owners' residual interest (capital, retained earnings, owner draws, dividends declared charged to equity, treasury stock).
criteria.revenue: Income earned from operations or other gains, and contra-revenue such as sales returns.
criteria.expense: Operating costs other than cost of goods sold (wages, rent, depreciation, insurance expense, freight-out).
criteria.cogs: Cost of the goods sold, plus purchases and freight-in under the PERIODIC inventory system.

cases.title: Prepaid insurance paid
cases.input: On 1 July the company paid $12,000 cash for a 12-month insurance policy. Classify the debit side.
cases.rationale: The debit goes to Prepaid Insurance, an asset that is expensed over the policy term.

cases.title: Customer pays in advance
cases.input: A customer paid $3,000 in advance for services to be delivered next quarter. Classify the credit side.
cases.rationale: The credit goes to Unearned Revenue, an obligation to perform, not revenue yet.

cases.title: Owner withdraws cash
cases.input: The sole proprietor withdrew $2,000 cash for personal use. Classify the debit side.
cases.rationale: The debit goes to Owner's Drawings, which reduces equity; it is not an expense.

cases.title: Accrued wages at period end
cases.input: At year end, employees have earned $5,400 of wages that will be paid next week. Classify the credit side of the adjusting entry.
cases.rationale: The credit goes to Wages Payable (accrued wages), a liability. The debit side would be wages expense.

cases.title: Freight-in under periodic system
cases.input: The company uses the PERIODIC inventory system. It paid $450 to a carrier to deliver merchandise purchased for resale. Classify the debit side.
cases.rationale: Rule: under the periodic system freight-in is a cost of purchases and is classified as cogs (not asset and not freight-out expense).

cases.title: Accumulated depreciation (contra-asset)
cases.input: Classify the account named "Accumulated Depreciation - Equipment".
cases.rationale: A contra account takes the class of the account it offsets; it is a credit-balance contra-asset, not an expense or liability.

cases.title: Sales returns and allowances
cases.input: Classify the account named "Sales Returns and Allowances".
cases.rationale: It is a contra-revenue account, so it takes the revenue class rather than expense.

cases.title: Dividends declared, credit side
cases.input: On 15 December the board declared a $10,000 cash dividend payable on 15 January. Classify the credit side of the declaration entry.
cases.rationale: Once declared the company owes the dividend: Dividends Payable (liability). The debit side (retained earnings/dividends) is equity.

cases.title: Deferred tax liability
cases.input: Classify the account named "Deferred Tax Liability".
cases.rationale: Despite the word 'tax', it is a balance-sheet obligation, not an expense.

cases.title: Account lookup (templated)
cases.expected_expr: ({'Prepaid Rent':'asset','Unearned Revenue':'liability','Common Stock':'equity','Service Revenue':'revenue','Rent Expense':'expense','Cost of Goods Sold':'cogs','Accounts Receivable':'asset','Retained Earnings':'equity'})[vars.acct]
cases.rationale: Standard classes for each named account.

cases.title: Perpetual purchase on account (templated side)
cases.input: The company uses the PERPETUAL inventory system. It bought $5,000 of merchandise for resale on account from a supplier. Classify the {{side}} side.
cases.rationale: Perpetual: debit is Inventory (asset), credit is Accounts Payable (liability). Not cogs: nothing has been sold.

cases.title: Year-end depreciation entry (templated side)
cases.input: Record annual depreciation of $8,000 on equipment. Classify the {{side}} side of the entry.
cases.rationale: Debit is Depreciation Expense (expense); credit is Accumulated Depreciation, a contra-asset classified as asset.
